mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS trend (3-month) is downward but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 2.0% in the past month, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases the risk-free rate and discount rate, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a severe economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE rising does not produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%), the economy is in a late-cycle expansion phase, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate continued corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past 3 months indicates a tightening labor market, which typically precedes a rise in wage inflation and corporate profit margin pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE trend (3-month) is downward but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% in the past month, it signals an overheated labor market that triggers central bank intervention, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0% but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO) and rising housing starts (HOUST) signals strong economic demand and supply growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy avoids a recession.
failure_condition: The joint condition of INDPRO rising and HOUST rising does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) rises above 105.0 in the past month, it signals robust manufacturing activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy shows resilience to potential headwinds.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 105.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
